chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) and said: 'O Commander of the Faithful, my wife breastfed a boy, and I swore by Allah that I will not have sexual relations with you until she weans him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ila' in reconciliation.'

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Amir al-Mu'minin: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.إِيلَاءٌ: Ila: An oath by which a husband abstains from sexual relations with his wife for four months or more.
key_terms.الْإِصْلَاحِ: Al-Islaah: Reconciliation or restoring the marital bond.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling of Ila (oath of abstention) when a husband swears to abstain until his wife weans her child?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the specific form of *Ila'* where a husband swears to abstain until a specific event (such as weaning) does not preclude *Islaah* (reconciliation), allowing the couple to resume normal marital relations despite the oath. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic distinction between *Ila'* as a distinct vow requiring waiting periods and *Islaah* as a mechanism for restoring marital harmony without the strict constraints of the vow, reflecting the practical flexibility in family law. It underscores the principle that the intent of reconciliation takes precedence over the literal enforcement of the oath in this context.
